card.name: Is/are after a drug name, before metabolism
card.fires_on: The verb "is" or "are" (or "a"/"an" after it) right after a drug name, at the start of a statement about how the drug is metabolized, cleared or removed.

modes.label: Verb after drug name
modes.description: "is" or "are" directly after a drug name, leading into a metabolism or elimination statement.
modes.example: Cyclosporine<< is>> extensively metabolized by the liver.

modes.label: Article before enzyme role
modes.description: "a" or "an" after "is" or a comma, leading into a substrate, inducer or inhibitor role.
modes.example: Rosuvastatin is<< a>> substrate of CYP2C9 and

card.writes: It promotes adverbs of frequency like "commonly" and "rare" and suppresses "frequent", which suggests a word describing how often or how widely something occurs.
card.plain: It fires on the small word after a drug's name when the label starts to say how the drug is metabolized or cleared.
